item.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting. The crucial components of the proof are a long-time Egorov's theorem designed for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle of Cohen--Dyatlov [arXiv:2609.30261], and an application of Weyl's method for exponential sums.
item.dc:creator: Alex Cohen, Zhenhao Li, Zhongkai Tao

item.title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.36212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator. We also study the symplectization of curl eigenforms as a possible bridge to symplectic dynamics. Finally, we characterize those transversely vanishing $1$-forms which are curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric. We deduce a generalization of the classical correspondence, due to Etnyre and Ghrist, between Reeb-like fields of contact forms and nowhere-vanishing rotational Beltrami fields to the setting of transversely vanishing vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cardona, Willi Kepplinger

item.title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.36240v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - V\beta$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.
item.dc:creator: David Gontier, Hanne Van Den Bosch

item.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.36403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schr\"odinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.
item.dc:creator: David Damanik (Rice University), Long Li (Texas A&M University), Nicolae Strungaru (MacEwan University)

item.title: Threshold Criteria for Bosonic and Fermionic Trimers on a Square Lattice: A Birman--Schwinger Comparison
item.description: arXiv:2610.37142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compare two three-particle lattice models on the square lattice at total quasimomentum zero: three identical bosons with attractive contact interactions, and a two-fermion plus one distinguishable particle system with attractive interspecies contact. Using the Birman--Schwinger principle combined with symmetry reduction and strong-coupling asymptotics, we distinguish shared methodology from model-dependent spectral conclusions. For bosons, the ground-state energy behaves as minus three times the coupling plus six minus three over twice the coupling plus higher-order corrections, and exactly two bound states exist below the threshold for large coupling; the second lies at a finite distance 0.03542 below the threshold, a genuine eigenvalue rather than a threshold resonance. For fermions, the critical mass ratio is pi divided by pi minus two, approximately 2.75194; above it, a doubly degenerate level appears at strong coupling. Near onset, the binding energy follows a linear-over-logarithmic law. The results are compared with numerical finite-grid Faddeev computations and with recent three-dimensional classifications of threshold states.
item.dc:creator: Janikul Abdullaev, Abdumalik Eshniyozov, Mikhail Dolgopolov

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Sharp Poincar\'e inequality for $W_0^{2,p}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37433v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The first eigenvalue of the $p$-bilaplacian over a domain $\Omega$ is the inverse of the Poincar\'e constant for $W_0^{2,p}(\Omega)$. In dimension two, we prove that it is minimised by disks under area constraint, thereby obtaining a sharp uniform Poincar\'e inequality.
item.dc:creator: Rom\'eo Leylekian

item.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.37463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Jiaoyang Huang, Ruizhe Xu

item.title: Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37479v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In his global theory of one-frequency Schr\"odinger operators~\cite{Av15}, Avila asked whether the acceleration of a real-analytic $\SL(2,\R)$ cocycle over an irrational circle rotation is bounded below by the absolute value of its topological degree and whether equality in nonzero degree characterizes premonotonicity. We answer this question affirmatively for every irrational frequency, without arithmetic restrictions. Here premonotonicity means that some iterate becomes strictly monotonic in the base variable after a periodic change of coordinates~\cite{AK15}. In the positive Lyapunov exponent regime, this provides a nonzero-degree counterpart to Avila's characterization of uniform hyperbolicity by vanishing acceleration. In nonzero degree, we also characterize minimal acceleration through signed connections and invariant positive matrix-valued measures. In the positive-degree, positive Lyapunov exponent case, the proof constructs an analytic positive connection using invariant positive matrix-valued measures and a transfer--scattering representation. A complex-analytic construction then produces a periodic gauge. As a further consequence, for each fixed irrational frequency and nonzero degree, the premonotonic locus is path connected: every cocycle in this locus can be joined to the linear rotation of the same degree by a path preserving premonotonicity.
item.dc:creator: Xu Xia, Jiahao Xu

item.title: Every route counts, but some count more: a max-plus view of the C. elegans brain
item.description: arXiv:2610.37587v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Brains do not simply add up every signal they receive: they select which routes dominate. Yet connectomes are usually analyzed with tools that sum over all paths and place neural states in Euclidean spaces, blurring the feedback circuits that may sustain internal states. Here we treat neural signaling as routing instead of diffusion and describe it with max-plus algebra, in which signals accumulate along a path and the strongest route prevails. We propose a model in which the functional connectome of Caenorhabditis elegans emerges from the time-varying combination of electrical, synaptic, monoaminergic, neuropeptidergic and hormonal layers, and analyze five networks within this framework. Each collapses onto a handful of dominant feedback loops, which recover well-characterized circuits and point to new candidates for experimental study. Unlike linear spectra, these structures keep the biological meaning of the data, and their order-based description suggests that brain states live in lattices rather than Euclidean spaces.
item.dc:creator: Emma Reyner-Fuentes, Sebastian Rudolph, Carmen Pel\'aez-Moreno, Francisco J. Valverde-Albacete

item.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
item.description: arXiv:2408.09238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.
item.dc:creator: Illya Koval, Amir Vig

item.title: Reconstruction of Heat Geometry from a Scalar Process
item.description: arXiv:2609.27967v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A smooth scalar process with one fixed Gaussian covariance kernel determines any finite graded family of symmetric Hilbert tensors up to a common orthogonal isomorphism of their minimal supports. For two heat tensors, its law determines a closed positive-dimensional Riemannian manifold, a Euclidean bundle, its connection and potential, and the unknown heat time, up to isometry and gauge. The quadratic tensor recovers the scaled generator; the quartic tensor recovers the spatial norm and volume, which fix the time scale. For compact finite-dimensional RCD spaces, the same law determines the measured space with distance divided by the square root of the heat time.
item.dc:creator: Obayda Julien Assaad
